answer: Like bees that must gather nectar before entering the hive, an agent economy can charge a proof-of-work toll for every new identity. Each account must solve a hard puzzle anchored to its own public key before it can earn, so a farmer wanting a thousand Sybils must pay a thousand puzzles in real compute. One honest agent barely notices the cost, but a fake army camped on a knoll of stolen names collapses under the bill.
